_doc: Tier A coverage map (in-place-image-convergence 1.2). One entry per tier A destination of image-files.manifest. level behaviour: committing the evidence mutation of src makes the named accepted fixture(s) FAIL in gate/shadow-eval.sh; parse: only a syntax mutation does; none: no fixture fails. pull-sync (in-place-image-convergence 1.3) installs a tooling path in place only at level behaviour and only when the staged blob equals src_blob, or while it is listed in an unexpired converges_today_exempt (through its expires day, UTC); everything else stays as baked and is converged by the image. reason for none: outside-gate-paths (src is not a gate path), converges-today-uncovered (pull-sync installs it today with no fixture; listed in converges_today_exempt), unreached (baked only). src_blob is the git blob the proof ran on; a live src blob that differs means the proof is older than the code: for a behaviour entry that freezes the path, so image-coverage-map.test.sh fails on it; refresh the hashes with validation/scripts/coverage-refresh-behaviour-blobs.sh --write and re-earn the proof with image-coverage-map.check.sh in the same commit. Kept consistent by validation/scripts/image-coverage-map.test.sh; proofs re-run by image-coverage-map.check.sh. A parse entry under the units dir converges in place today without a behaviour proof, so it is listed in converges_today_exempt too (debt, dated): for a unit file the exit-99 mutation is a syntax mutation, and only a semantic mutant failing a fixture earns behaviour.

converges_today_exempt.reason: converges today; gated as fixtures earn coverage

tier_b._doc: Tier B (in-place-image-convergence 2.4): the baked copy of scripts/substrate (/usr/local/share/substrate/super-repo/scripts/substrate) that the federation transport and relay run from. pull-sync's converge_tier_b converges it in place from the ACCEPTED gate only while this record names at least one behaviour fixture and the accepted corpus (validation/scripts/gate/fixtures/) holds each one; otherwise the tree stays as baked and the tick says held. A fixture is named by its file name. The relay fixture is the one that judges the tree by what it carries (large noise frames over two circuits); the transport server is not run by any fixture, so the readiness check after its restart (health, start time, loaded hash) is its only judge. Removing a name here holds the tree again.
